hindi: अथवा उसके सार बल को वमन कराकर प्रहार करे।
english: Or, having caused his strong force to vomit out, he should strike [it].
notes: vamayitvā is the causative of √vam, literally "having made (it) vomit out"; the sense is probably "having made the force come out (of the fort)", but the text gives only the literal verb. Object of abhihanyāt is not stated. sāra-bala rendered "strong force" as in the glossary (10.5).
lines_deva: सार.बलं वा-अस्य वमयित्वा-अभिहन्यात्
lines_iast: sāra.balaṃ vā-asya vamayitvā-abhihanyāt

words.gloss: those submitting with their army, and forest chiefs

hindi: इससे सेना सहित समर्पण करने वाले और आटविक समझाए गए हैं।
english: By this, those submitting with their army and the forest chiefs are explained.
notes: tena refers back to the method just described. daṇḍa-upanata and āṭavika are taken as two classes joined in a dvandva.
lines_deva: तेन दण्ड.उपनत.आटविका व्याख्याताः
lines_iast: tena daṇḍa.upanata.āṭavikā vyākhyātāḥ

words.gloss: of the two: one submitting with army, forest chief

hindi: अथवा सेना सहित समर्पण करने वाले और आटविक, इन दोनों में से कोई एक, घिरे हुए के पास भेजे – “यह घेरा डालने वाला रोगी है, पार्ष्णिग्राह से आक्रान्त है, दूसरा छिद्र उत्पन्न हो गया है, दूसरी भूमि में हट जाना चाहता है।”
english: Or one of the two – [the one] submitting with [his] army, or the forest chief – should send [word] to the besieged: “This besieger is sick, attacked by a heel-seizer; another weak point has arisen; [he is] desirous of retreating to another ground.”
notes: preṣayet has no stated object; the quotation is the message. chidra literally "opening, hole"; rendered "weak point". The e-text writes sam- (samruddha, samroddhā) for saṃ-; this is the e-text convention (also sampīḍana), not flagged. The quoted message closes with the quotation mark only (glossary).
lines_deva: दण्ड.उपनत.आटविकयोर् अन्यतरो वा सम्रुद्धस्य प्रेषयेत् - "अयं सम्रोद्धा व्याधितः, पार्ष्णि.ग्राहेण-अभियुक्तः, छिद्रम् अन्यद् उत्थितम्, अन्यस्यां भूमाव् अपयातु.कामः" इति
lines_iast: daṇḍa.upanata.āṭavikayor anyataro vā samruddhasya preṣayet - "ayaṃ samroddhā vyādhitaḥ, pārṣṇi.grāheṇa-abhiyuktaḥ, chidram anyad utthitam, anyasyāṃ bhūmāv apayātu.kāmaḥ" iti

hindi: स्वीकार कर लिए जाने पर घेरा डालने वाला स्कन्धावार को जलाकर हट जाए।
english: When [it] has been accepted, the besieger, having set fire to the camp, should retreat.
notes: pratipanne is a locative absolute with no stated subject (presumably the besieged who has accepted the message of the previous unit); "accepted" is the literal sense of prati-√pad pp, alternative "agreed/believed". skandhāvāra = camp (glossary).
lines_deva: प्रतिपन्ने सम्रोद्धा स्कन्ध.आवारम् आदीप्य-अपयायात्
lines_iast: pratipanne samroddhā skandha.āvāram ādīpya-apayāyāt

hindi: तब पहले की तरह आचरण करे।
english: Then he should act as before.
lines_deva: ततः पूर्ववद् आचरेत्
lines_iast: tataḥ pūrvavad ācaret

hindi: अथवा माल का सम्पात करके विष-मिले माल से इसे छल ले।
english: Or, having made a passage of merchandise, he should outwit him with merchandise mixed with poison.
notes: sampāta (lit. "falling/coming together, passing") in paṇya-sampāta is obscure; rendered literally "passage of merchandise"; the alternative is "arrival/inflow of goods". rasa = poison (glossary). atisandadhyāt rendered "outwit" as in the glossary (atisaṃhita). Hindi keeps सम्पात as the Sanskrit word; no sure Hindi equivalent is known. Reviewer: sense of paṇya-sampāta uncertain, a person should check it against a commentary.
lines_deva: पण्य.सम्पातं वा कृत्वा पण्येन-एनं रस.विद्धेन-अतिसन्दध्यात्
lines_iast: paṇya.sampātaṃ vā kṛtvā paṇyena-enaṃ rasa.viddhena-atisandadhyāt

words.gloss: one in the guise of a reinforcer

hindi: अथवा आसार का रूप धारण किया हुआ घिरे हुए के पास दूत भेजे – “मेरे द्वारा बाहरी पर प्रहार किया गया है, प्रहार करने के लिए निकल आओ।”
english: Or one in the guise of a reinforcer should send a messenger to the besieged: “The outer [force] has been struck by me; go out to strike.”
notes: bāhyam abhihatam is neuter and has no stated noun; "[force]" is supplied. Alternative: "the outside has been struck". āsāra = reinforcer (glossary); X-vyañjana = in the guise of X (12.5).
lines_deva: आसार.व्यञ्जनो वा सम्रुद्धस्य दूतं प्रेषयेत् - "मया बाह्यम् अभिहतम् उपनिर्गच्छ-अभिहन्तुम्" इति
lines_iast: āsāra.vyañjano vā samruddhasya dūtaṃ preṣayet - "mayā bāhyam abhihatam upanirgaccha-abhihantum" iti

hindi: स्वीकार कर लेने वाले के प्रति पहले की तरह आचरण करे।
english: He should act as before towards the one who has accepted.
notes: "towards" is supplied for the accusative object of ācaret; pratipanna as in 36.
lines_deva: प्रतिपन्नं पूर्ववद् आचरेत्
lines_iast: pratipannaṃ pūrvavad ācaret

words.gloss: with order and pass in hand

hindi: मित्र अथवा बन्धु को बहाना बनाकर, आदेश और मुद्रा हाथ में लिए हुए गुप्त पुरुष प्रवेश करके दुर्ग को हस्तगत करवाएँ।
english: Having made an ally or a kinsman their pretext, the secret agents, with order and pass in hand, having entered, should have the fort seized.
notes: apadiśya: apa-√diś is "to allege, give as pretext"; the exact pretext (e.g. that they come from the ally or kinsman) is not stated, so only the literal phrase is given; medium/low. śāsana-mudrā may also be one compound idea "the pass of the order". The causative grāhayeyuḥ has no stated agent of seizing. yoga-puruṣa = secret agent, mudrā = pass (glossary).
lines_deva: मित्रं बन्धुं वा-अपदिश्य योग.पुरुषाः शासन.मुद्रा.हस्ताः प्रविश्य दुर्गं ग्राहयेयुः
lines_iast: mitraṃ bandhuṃ vā-apadiśya yoga.puruṣāḥ śāsana.mudrā.hastāḥ praviśya durgaṃ grāhayeyuḥ

words.gloss: one in the guise of a reinforcer

hindi: अथवा आसार का रूप धारण किया हुआ घिरे हुए के पास भेजे – “अमुक स्थान और समय पर मैं स्कन्धावार पर प्रहार करूँगा, तुम्हें भी युद्ध करना चाहिए।”
english: Or one in the guise of a reinforcer should send [word] to the besieged: “At such-and-such a place and time I shall strike the camp; you also must fight.”

text_flags.why: Extra ñ: the word is vyañjana (as in units 39 and 46); the Devanagari व्यञ्ज्ञनो shows the same doubling.

notes: yoddhavyam is an impersonal gerundive with instrumental: "it is to be fought by you". Whose camp is meant is not stated.
lines_deva: आसार.व्यञ्ज्ञनो वा सम्रुद्धस्य प्रेषयेत् - "अमुष्मिन् देशे काले च स्कन्ध.आवारम् अभिहनिष्यामि, युष्माभिर् अपि योद्धव्यम्" इति
lines_iast: āsāra.vyañjñano vā samruddhasya preṣayet - "amuṣmin deśe kāle ca skandha.āvāram abhihaniṣyāmi, yuṣmābhir api yoddhavyam" iti

hindi: स्वीकार कर लेने वाले को, जैसा कहा गया है वैसे, आक्रमण से व्याकुल दिखाकर, रात में दुर्ग से निकले हुए को मरवाए।
english: Having shown, as stated, [it] in confusion from the attack to the one who has accepted, he should have him killed when he has come out of the fort at night.
notes: The noun qualified by abhyāghāta-saṅkulam is not stated (probably the camp of the previous units); "[it]" is supplied. The accusative pair pratipannam ... niṣkrāntam is read as one person, the object of ghātayet; "when" renders the participle niṣkrāntam. Low-medium certainty on the syntax.
lines_deva: प्रतिपन्नं यथा.उक्तम् अभ्याघात.सङ्कुलं दर्शयित्वा रात्रौ दुर्गान् निष्क्रान्तं घातयेत्
lines_iast: pratipannaṃ yathā.uktam abhyāghāta.saṅkulaṃ darśayitvā rātrau durgān niṣkrāntaṃ ghātayet

hindi: अथवा जिस मित्र को या आटविक को बुलाए, उसे प्रोत्साहित करे – “आक्रमण करके, घिरे होने पर इसकी भूमि ले लो।”
english: Or the ally, or the forest chief, whom he summons – him he should encourage: “Having attacked while [he is] besieged, take his land.”

text_flags.why: Possible typo (doubled v); the word is āṭavika, as elsewhere in the chunk (Devanagari आटव्विकं shows the same).

notes: yat is taken as a neuter relative agreeing with mitram. saṃruddhe is read as a locative absolute ("while he is besieged"); alternative: "against the besieged". vikramya = "having attacked" (cf. glossary vikramayet).
lines_deva: यद् वा मित्रम् आवाहयेद् आटव्विकं वा, तम् उत्साहयेत् "विक्रम्य सम्रुद्धे भूमिम् अस्य प्रतिपद्यस्व" इति
lines_iast: yad vā mitram āvāhayed āṭavvikaṃ vā, tam utsāhayet "vikramya samruddhe bhūmim asya pratipadyasva" iti

words.gloss: by winning over the treasonable and chiefs

hindi: आक्रमण करने वाले को प्रकृतियों द्वारा, या दूष्यों और मुख्यों को अपने पक्ष में करके मरवाए; अथवा “यह मित्र का घातक है” ऐसा कहकर, अपना प्रयोजन पा लेने पर, स्वयं विष से मरवाए।
english: He should have the one who has attacked killed through the constituent elements, or by winning over the treasonable and the chiefs; or himself with poison, [saying] “This one is a killer of an ally”, his aim having been gained.
notes: upagraha literally "seizing, taking hold"; "winning over" is the usual sense and is medium confidence. prakṛtibhiḥ is kept as "constituent elements" (glossary); alternative "subjects". The word "[saying]" is supplied for iti; the verb of svayaṃ vā rasena is understood from ghātayet.
lines_deva: विक्रान्तं प्रकृतिभिर् दूष्य.मुख्य.उपग्रहेण वा घातयेत्, स्वयं वा रसेन "मित्र.घातको ऽयम्" इत्य् अवाप्त.अर्थः
lines_iast: vikrāntaṃ prakṛtibhir dūṣya.mukhya.upagraheṇa vā ghātayet, svayaṃ vā rasena "mitra.ghātako 'yam" ity avāpta.arthaḥ

words.gloss: one in the guise of an ally

hindi: अथवा मित्र का रूप धारण किया हुआ, आक्रमण करने की इच्छा वाले की शत्रु के पास शिकायत करे।
english: Or one in the guise of an ally should denounce the one desirous of attacking [to] the enemy.
notes: The construction of parasya with abhiśaṃset is unclear (genitive of the person addressed, "to the enemy", versus "of the enemy"); "[to]" is supplied. abhi-√śaṃs = accuse, denounce; alternative "report". Low-medium certainty. Reviewer: the genitive of the recipient after a verb of sending/telling occurs in this chunk (saṃruddhasya preṣayet, units 35, 39, 42), which supports 'to the enemy'.
lines_deva: विक्रमितु.कामं वा मित्र.व्यञ्जनः परस्य-अभिशंसेत्
lines_iast: vikramitu.kāmaṃ vā mitra.vyañjanaḥ parasya-abhiśaṃset

words.gloss: having attained the state of a trusted one
words.gram: m. nom. sg. ppp. (tat-puruṣa: acc. + ppp.)

hindi: विश्वसनीय की स्थिति पा लेने पर उसके वीर पुरुषों को मरवा डाले।
english: Having attained the state of a trusted one, he should have his brave men slain.

text_flags.why: Possible missing space: puruṣān and asya are separate words; the e-text runs them together.

notes: āpta literally "reliable, trusted (or attained)"; subject and the person who trusts (presumably the enemy) are not stated. upaghāta literally "injury, destruction".
lines_deva: आप्त.भाव.उपगतः प्रवीर.पुरुषानस्य-उपघातयेत्
lines_iast: āpta.bhāva.upagataḥ pravīra.puruṣānasya-upaghātayet

hindi: अथवा सन्धि करके इसे जनपद में बसाए।
english: Or, having made a treaty, he should cause him to settle [in] the country.
notes: niveśayet is causative with a double accusative; "[in]" is supplied. Whether it means "settle him in the country" or "make him settle (populate) the country" is not decided by the line (compare niviṣṭam in 49).
lines_deva: सन्धिं वा कृत्वा जन.पदम् एनं निवेशयेत्
lines_iast: sandhiṃ vā kṛtvā jana.padam enaṃ niveśayet

hindi: अज्ञात रहकर उसके बसे हुए जनपद पर प्रहार करे।
english: Unrecognised, he should strike his settled country.
notes: asya is taken as "of him" (the enemy of 48); niviṣṭa "settled" could also be "encamped, occupied".
lines_deva: निविष्टम् अस्य जन.पदम् अविज्ञातो हन्यात्
lines_iast: niviṣṭam asya jana.padam avijñāto hanyāt

words.gloss: having caused a wrong to be done
among the treasonable and forest chiefs

hindi: दूष्यों और आटविकों के विषय में अपकार करवाकर, अथवा सेना का एक भाग पार ले जाकर, दुर्ग को आक्रमण द्वारा छिनवा ले।
english: Having caused a wrong to be done in the case of the treasonable and the forest chiefs, or having led across one part of the army, he should have the fort taken by assault.
notes: Obscure. dūṣya-āṭavikeṣu may instead go with atinīya ("led across to the treasonable and forest chiefs"); apakārayitvā has no stated object. Both are rendered literally. avaskanda = assault (glossary).
lines_deva: अपकारयित्वा दूष्य.आटविकेषु वा बल.एक.देशम् अतिनीय दुर्गम् अवस्कन्देन हारयेत्
lines_iast: apakārayitvā dūṣya.āṭavikeṣu vā bala.eka.deśam atinīya durgam avaskandena hārayet

words.gloss: treasonable, enemies, forest chiefs, hated, withdrawn
having wealth and honour made, with signals and marks

hindi: दूष्य, शत्रु, आटविक, द्वेष्य और लौटे हुए, जिन्हें धन और मान दिया गया है तथा जो संकेत और चिह्न वाले हैं, शत्रु के दुर्ग पर आक्रमण करें।
english: The treasonable, enemies, forest chiefs, the hated, and those who have withdrawn, having had wealth and honour made [for them], with signals and marks, should assault the enemy's fort.
notes: Obscure: kṛta-artha-māna read as "to whom wealth and honour have been made (given)"; alternative "whose purpose and honour have been accomplished". sañjñā-cihna = signals and marks (of recognition); dveṣya = "hateful, hated" (by whom is not stated); pratyapasṛta = "gone back, withdrawn". amitra = enemy (glossary).
lines_deva: दूष्य.अमित्र.आटविक.द्वेष्य.प्रत्यपसृताश् च कृत.अर्थ.मान.सञ्ज्ञा.चिह्नाः पर.दुर्गम् अवस्कन्देयुः
lines_iast: dūṣya.amitra.āṭavika.dveṣya.pratyapasṛtāś ca kṛta.artha.māna.sañjñā.cihnāḥ para.durgam avaskandeyuḥ

words.gloss: the fallen, the turned away, the surrendered (continues in the next word)
words.gram: m. (dvandva members, dative pl. completed in the next word)

words.gloss: to those with loosed hair and weapons, the frightened, the disfigured
words.gram: m. dat. pl. (dvandva, continuing the previous word)

hindi: शत्रु के दुर्ग अथवा स्कन्धावार पर आक्रमण करके, गिरे हुए, मुँह फेरे हुए, समर्पण करने वाले, खुले केश और छोड़े हुए शस्त्र वाले, भयभीत, विकृत रूप वाले और युद्ध न करने वालों को अभय दें।
english: Having assaulted the enemy's fort or camp, they should give safety to those fallen, turned away or surrendered, and to those with loosed hair and weapons, the frightened, the disfigured, and to those not fighting.

text_flags.why: One slip explains two oddities: the m of mukta has moved onto the previous word (abhipanna+m / m+ukta -> abhipannam ukta). Restored, ukta (no sense with keśa-śastra) becomes mukta (loosed, dropped) and abhipannam (an accusative where abhayam dadyuḥ needs a dative) becomes the stem abhipanna, so patita-parāṅmukha-abhipanna-mukta-keśa-śastra-bhaya-virūpebhyaḥ is one dative dvandva with ayudhyamānebhyaḥ. The Devanagari repeats the e-text.

notes: Translation follows two emendations that come from one slip in the e-text: the m of mukta has moved onto the previous word (abhipannam ukta for abhipanna mukta), so the text is read patita-parāṅmukha-abhipanna-mukta-keśa-śastra-bhaya-virūpebhyaḥ, one dative dvandva, all recipients of abhayam together with ayudhyamānebhyaḥ. abhipanna is rendered "surrendered" (literally "approached, come to"; abhi-√pad can also mean overcome or afflicted), medium-low confidence. mukta-keśa-śastra is read as mukta applying to both keśa and śastra (loosed hair, dropped weapons). bhaya-virūpa read as "frightened" and "disfigured". The sentence could also be read with skandhāvāraṃ vā patita-... as one phrase; the former reading is used.
lines_deva: पर.दुर्गम् अवस्कन्द्य स्कन्ध.आवारं वा पतित.परान्.मुख.अभिपन्नम् उक्त.केश.शस्त्र.भय.विरूपेभ्यश् च-अभयम् अयुध्यमानेभ्यश् च दद्युः
lines_iast: para.durgam avaskandya skandha.āvāraṃ vā patita.parān.mukha.abhipannam ukta.keśa.śastra.bhaya.virūpebhyaś ca-abhayam ayudhyamānebhyaś ca dadyuḥ

words.gloss: with secret punishment and remedying done

hindi: शत्रु के दुर्ग को पाकर, जिसमें शत्रु-पक्ष शुद्ध कर दिया गया हो और गुप्त दण्ड तथा प्रतीकार कर लिया गया हो, भीतर और बाहर प्रवेश करे।
english: Having obtained the enemy's fort – with the enemy party cleared, with secret punishment and remedying done – he should enter [it], inside and outside.
notes: The two long compounds are taken as adjectives of para-durgam. upāṃśu-daṇḍa-pratīkāra may also be read as two items, "secret punishment" and "remedying". "Inside and outside" with praviśet is literal; the sense (e.g. entering both inner and outer parts) is not spelled out. daṇḍa here = punishment (not army).
lines_deva: पर.दुर्गम् अवाप्य विशुद्ध.शत्रु.पक्षं कृत.उपांशु.दण्ड.प्रतीकारम् अन्तर्.बहिश् च प्रविशेत्
lines_iast: para.durgam avāpya viśuddha.śatru.pakṣaṃ kṛta.upāṃśu.daṇḍa.pratīkāram antar.bahiś ca praviśet

hindi: इस प्रकार विजिगीषु शत्रु की भूमि पा लेने पर मध्यम को पाना चाहे; उसकी सिद्धि होने पर उदासीन को।
english: Thus the conqueror, having obtained the enemy's land, should seek to gain the middle king; on success in that, the neutral king.
notes: lipseta is the desiderative of √labh, "should seek to gain". The second clause omits the verb (lipseta is understood). bhūmi rendered "land" here, not "ground" (battle ground).
lines_deva: एवं विजिगीषुर् अमित्र.भूमिं लब्ध्वा मध्यमं लिप्सेत, तत्.सिद्धाव् उदासीनम्
lines_iast: evaṃ vijigīṣur amitra.bhūmiṃ labdhvā madhyamaṃ lipseta, tat.siddhāv udāsīnam

hindi: पृथ्वी को जीतने का यह पहला मार्ग है।
english: This is the first way to conquer the earth.
lines_deva: एष प्रथमो मार्गः पृथिवीं जेतुम्
lines_iast: eṣa prathamo mārgaḥ pṛthivīṃ jetum

words.gloss: of the middle and the neutral king

hindi: मध्यम और उदासीन के अभाव में गुणों की श्रेष्ठता से शत्रु-प्रकृतियों को वश में करे, फिर आगे की प्रकृतियों को।
english: In the absence of the middle and the neutral king, he should subdue the enemy constituents through superiority in qualities, then the subsequent constituents.
notes: ari-prakṛti is rendered literally "enemy constituents" (here presumably the members of the circle of kings that are enemies); the sense is not spelled out. sādhayet "should subdue" (lit. "cause to be accomplished"); the second clause omits the verb. atiśaya here "superiority", not the battle sense "special advantage".
lines_deva: मध्यम.उदासीनयोर् अभावे गुण.अतिशयेन-अरि.प्रकृतीः साधयेत्, तत उत्तराः प्रकृतीः
lines_iast: madhyama.udāsīnayor abhāve guṇa.atiśayena-ari.prakṛtīḥ sādhayet, tata uttarāḥ prakṛtīḥ

hindi: यह दूसरा मार्ग है।
english: This is the second way.
lines_deva: एष द्वितीयो मार्गः
lines_iast: eṣa dvitīyo mārgaḥ

hindi: मण्डल के अभाव में शत्रु के द्वारा मित्र को अथवा मित्र के द्वारा शत्रु को दोनों ओर से दबाकर वश में करे।
english: In the absence of a circle, he should subdue an ally by means of an enemy, or an enemy by means of an ally, by pressing from both sides.
notes: maṇḍala = circle (glossary). mitra = ally, never "friend".
lines_deva: मण्डलस्य-अभावे शत्रुणा मित्रं मित्रेण वा शत्रुम् उभयतः.सम्पीडनेन साधयेत्
lines_iast: maṇḍalasya-abhāve śatruṇā mitraṃ mitreṇa vā śatrum ubhayataḥ.sampīḍanena sādhayet

hindi: यह तीसरा मार्ग है।
english: This is the third way.

text_flags.why: Possible typo: "." marks a compound junction, but eṣaḥ and tṛtīyaḥ are two separate words (cf. eṣa dvitīyo in unit 57).

lines_deva: एष.तृतीयो मार्गः
lines_iast: eṣa.tṛtīyo mārgaḥ

hindi: अथवा किसी एक शक्य पड़ोसी को वश में करे; उसके साथ दुगुना होकर दूसरे को और तिगुना होकर तीसरे को वश में करे।
english: Or he should subdue one feasible neighbour; with him, twofold [in strength], [he should subdue] the second, [and] threefold, the third.
notes: śakya "feasible, possible (to subdue)"; the verb of the second half is understood from sādhayet (Hindi repeats it to complete the sentence). dvi-guṇa/tri-guṇa "twofold/threefold" is read of the conqueror's strength after gaining the first neighbour; the text does not say "strength". Medium-low certainty.
lines_deva: शक्यम् एकं वा सामन्तं साधयेत्, तेन द्वि.गुणो द्वितीयम्, त्रि.गुणस् तृतीयम्
lines_iast: śakyam ekaṃ vā sāmantaṃ sādhayet, tena dvi.guṇo dvitīyam, tri.guṇas tṛtīyam

hindi: पृथ्वी को जीतने का यह चौथा मार्ग है।
english: This is the fourth way to conquer the earth.
lines_deva: एष चतुर्थो मार्गः पृथिवीं जेतुम्
lines_iast: eṣa caturtho mārgaḥ pṛthivīṃ jetum

hindi: पृथ्वी को जीतकर, जिसमें वर्ण और आश्रम विभक्त हैं, अपने धर्म से उसका उपभोग करे।
english: And having conquered the earth, with its varṇas and āśramas divided, he should enjoy [it] by his own dharma.
notes: bhuñjīta literally "should enjoy"; √bhuj can also mean "rule, govern". vibhakta "divided, apportioned"; alternative "distinguished". sva-dharma is "his own dharma" (the king's own), not specified further.
lines_deva: जित्वा च पृथिवीं विभक्त.वर्ण.आश्रमां स्व.धर्मेण भुञ्जीत
lines_iast: jitvā ca pṛthivīṃ vibhakta.varṇa.āśramāṃ sva.dharmeṇa bhuñjīta

words.gloss: of the obtaining of a fort

hindi: उपजाप, गुप्तचर, वमन कराना, घेरा डालना और कुचलना – ये पाँच दुर्ग की प्राप्ति के साधन हैं।
english: Secret instigation, spies, causing to vomit out, besieging and crushing – these five are the means of obtaining a fort.
notes: vāmana is a technical term, probably "luring the enemy out" (compare vamayitvā in unit 33), but only the literal sense "causing to vomit out" is given. paryupāsana literally "sitting around" = besieging; avamarda literally "crushing, trampling". hetu "cause, means". upajāpa = secret instigation, apasarpa = spy (glossary).
lines_deva: उपजापो ऽपसर्पश् च वामनं पर्युपासनम्
अवमर्दश् च पञ्च-एते दुर्ग.लम्भस्य हेतवः
lines_iast: upajāpo 'pasarpaś ca vāmanaṃ paryupāsanam
avamardaś ca pañca-ete durga.lambhasya hetavaḥ
